chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Remain in a state of purity after you have prayed the Fajr prayer, then stand; if you wish, stand near the mountain, and if you wish, stand where you spent the night. When you stand, praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and extol Him, and remember from His favors and blessings whatever you are able to, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Then let your words be: 'O Allah, Lord of the Sacred Mash'ar, free my neck from the Fire, and broaden for me from Your lawful provision, and avert from me the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humans. O Allah, You are the best of those sought, the best of those called upon, and the best of those asked. And every visitor has a right [of return], so make my right in this my station that You excuse my stumble, accept my excuse, and overlook my sin. Then make piety from the world my provision.'
Then proceed to where Thabir rises for you and you see the camels' footprints.
And it is recommended for the single pilgrim to tread the Sacred Mash'ar and to enter the House. He narrated that.

key_terms.اَلصَّرُورَةُ: The single pilgrim (one who has not brought a sacrificial animal)
key_terms.اَلْمَشْعَرُ اَلْحَرَامُ: The Sacred Mash'ar (a specific spot at Muzdalifah)
key_terms.رَبَّ اَلْمَشْعَرِ: Lord of the Mash'ar (addressing Allah in the supplication)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and etiquette for a pilgrim at Muzdalifah after the Fajr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the ritual of standing at Muzdalifah, emphasizing the transition from the sacred site of Mash'ar al-Haram to Mina while maintaining ritual purity. It highlights the scholarly tradition of reciting a specific du'a that links spiritual deliverance and divine provision to the physical act of pilgrimage, reinforcing the concept of *Taqwa* as the essential provision for the journey.
